facts.text: NanoDrop1000 is a USB device with VID 0x2457, PID 0x1002, a command endpoint, a spectrum endpoint and a text/status endpoint

connect() finds the device by VID/PID, sets its configuration, clears the three endpoint halts, sends the wake command 0x08 and the init command 0x01, then downloads the factory coefficients and calculates the wavelength axis
close() turns the lamp and magnet off, resets the USB device and disposes the USB resources
set_lamp(state) writes command 0x03 with 0xFF for on and 0x00 for off
set_magnet(state) writes command 0x0F with 0xFF for on and 0x00 for off
take_blank sets the magnet True before its dark reading, with the comment 'Arm down'
measure_absorbance sets the magnet True before its sample reading
set_integration_time(ms) documents the valid range 3 to 65535 ms, clamps outside it and writes command 0x02 with a 16-bit little-endian exposure
_calculate_x_axis builds a 2048-element wavelength array in nanometres from factory coefficients 1 through 4
get_raw_spectrum() flushes stale image data, writes command 0x09 and decodes 64 reads of 64 bytes into 2048 16-bit pixels
take_blank(integration_ms=20) acquires a dark frame with the lamp off, then a blank frame with the lamp on, and turns the lamp and magnet off afterwards

measure_absorbance(integration_ms=20) requires a stored dark and blank spectrum, arms the magnet, turns the lamp on, reads one frame and returns the wavelength axis with -log10((sample-dark)/(blank-dark))
The example script plots the active sensor area roughly from 220 nm to 750 nm
The installation guide says the NanoDrop uses an older USB 1.1 microcontroller and that its Python driver is installed with Zadig's libusb-win32 replacement
The PyLabRobot wrapper class ThermoFisherNanoDrop1000 constructs one ThermoFisherNanoDrop1000Driver and one absorbance backend sharing it
